key_insight: A weakly supervised AI model (MIMIC) can triage early mycosis fungoides from benign inflammatory skin diseases on biopsy slides with high sensitivity.
clinical_relevance: If used as an initial screening tool, it could reduce unnecessary ancillary testing while helping pathologists catch most true mycosis fungoides cases.
method: Trained on 3,339 whole-slide images from two Dutch centers using attention-based multiple-instance learning.
Externally validated on 371 slides from four independent European centers.
Compared against 11 pathologists in a blinded reader study and then tested in a held-out consecutive clinical cohort.
evidence_signal: In the held-out cohort, the updated model achieved AUROC 0.87 with 97.8% sensitivity and 50.2% specificity at a prespecified low-risk threshold.
watch_item: This is a triage aid, not a standalone diagnosis; performance may vary by site, case mix, and slide quality, so local validation is important before clinical use.
paper_title: Histological triage of early-stage mycosis fungoides using a weakly supervised deep learning-based model: a multicentre, external validation, and clinical utility study
